title: Auditing Attribution by Conditioning Provenance in Any-Stem Music Generation
subtitle: Audio examples for an anonymous submission under review.
overview_html: An any-stem model writes new instrument stems into an existing multi-track section, conditioned on a registered prompt excerpt per stem (timbre) and the registered context mix (harmony, tempo, key). The examples below show that its outputs trace to that conditioning audio.
footer_html: Anonymous submission. This page loads no external resources.

sections.title: Verdict procedure for the memorization audit
sections.intro_html: Figure 2 of the paper is the procedure behind every verdict, and its evidence for a reproduction is that the same material returns when the stem is generated again. Each card plays eight regenerations with the original context and eight with the context removed.

sections.title: Notes
sections.intro_html:
Each section is one float of the paper; the chip on a card is that card's identifier on this page.

All excerpts are capped at 20 s and provided solely for review purposes.

The model was trained on an in-house multi-track catalog of stems; no excerpt is a complete work.

Loudness is normalized per row (generated stems matched to the real stem), so level differences are not informative.
